Snapline 2.30.0

8 September 2026

  • Open from Clipboard: Annotate an image you copied from a browser, Slack, Figma or Messages without saving it first. Choose Open from Clipboard in the menu bar, press ⌃⌘V anywhere, or press ⌘V on the History shelf; while the clipboard holds an image, the shelf also offers a Paste from clipboard tile. The image becomes an ordinary capture: History, the Editor, text recognition, pinning and export all apply. The clipboard is read only when you ask and is never watched.
  • Done copies your annotations: Done in the Editor now saves the marked-up capture and puts it on the clipboard, ready to paste. Turn it off under Settings → General → After annotating.
  • Camera bubble in window recordings: The camera bubble is no longer disabled for window recordings. It is composited over the recorded window, and its preview follows the window as you move it.
  • Help: The feature tour now covers trim, GIF options, polygons, emoji stickers and Layers.

Snapline 2.29.0

7 September 2026

  • Licensing improvements: Activation, trials and the License settings pane are more reliable. A paid license keeps working offline as before; a trial now needs a brief moment online every few days.
  • Reset Activations: If a Mac you no longer use still holds a seat, the activation window can free all seats and activate here.
  • Under the hood: Stability and reliability fixes.

Snapline 2.28.0

6 September 2026

  • More reliable Tall Capture: Fixed captures stalling or ending halfway down pages with lazy-loading images or animated content. Matching now tolerates localized changes and recovers its position after a failed join. Repeated recoveries can keep extending the capture, including on pages with fixed bottom bars.
  • Full-width window captures: Fixed window captures losing their sidebars, margins or window controls. Tall Capture keeps the window’s full width and draws a fixed sidebar once, extending its background below it.
  • Cleaner sidebars: Fixed selected-item backgrounds and icon colors extending down long captures. Sidebar detection also handles edges that fall between matching blocks and continues working after a recovered join.

Show your clicks and keys in screen recordings

  • Highlight Clicks: every mouse click draws a brief expanding ring at the pointer — dual-tone, so it reads against any background. Display and region recordings.
  • Show Keystrokes: the keys you press appear in a capsule at the bottom of the movie, with shortcuts in the same ⌃⌥⇧⌘ symbols as the Shortcuts pane. Needs the Input Monitoring permission, asked once at the toggle; a recording never fails over it — refused access just means no capsule, and Snapline says so.
  • Both overlays are drawn into the recorded frames, so trims, GIF conversions, and shares keep them. The toggles live in the Record Screen bar and Settings → Recording, are remembered, and ship off. Worth knowing: Show Keystrokes records what you type — ordinary text included — into the video.

Snapline 2.16.0

Capture with Self-Timer: frame the region first, watch the countdown, and the shot fires by itself.

Capture

  • Capture with Self-Timer. Frame the region first, then a visible countdown runs — and the shot fires by itself. The delay is for staging: open the menu or tooltip you want inside the frame while the timer counts. Selection works exactly like a normal region capture (releasing the drag starts the timer — no extra confirm), and the countdown sits inside the region with the seconds, an Esc hint, and a ✕ to cancel. Nothing steals focus, so the menu you stage stays open, and the countdown never appears in the shot.
  • Pick 3, 5, or 10 seconds from the new status-menu item beside the Self-Timer setting — its top row remembers your last-used delay for a one-click repeat — or bind a shortcut in Settings → Shortcuts (it ships unbound). A canceled timer saves nothing and says so.
  • The invisible delay is gone. If you keep a sticky Self-Timer default set, region and main-display captures now show this same live countdown instead of silently stalling before the crosshair — same delay, visible and cancellable.

Snapline 2.15.0

History learns starred captures. The relaunch now waits for the old copy to actually exit.

History

  • History learns starred captures. Star anything worth keeping and it survives the retention sweep unconditionally — it never expires, and a starred card asks before a manual delete goes through. Star from the card's hover control or its Star/Unstar menu item; a starred capture wears a badge at rest. The History toolbar gains a Starred filter that combines with search.

Robustness

  • Fixed: Snapline could quit itself and not come back after you answered the Screen Recording prompt. The relaunch waited a fixed half-second before reopening, which could fire while the old copy was still shutting down — so nothing came back, and no crash report explained it. The relaunch now waits for the old copy to actually exit, and when it can't reopen safely it stays running and tells you instead of vanishing. The prompt for one permission no longer triggers a relaunch offer for another.
  • Also fixed: the camera bubble no longer scans for cameras on the main thread, which could stall the Record Screen bar (and probe for nearby iPhones) each time it opened; its window now closes cleanly instead of racing an in-flight animation; and the bubble's style controls no longer risk a crash from a settings change or a removed gradient stop.
